notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Matt Duchene is on long-term injured reserve (abdomen injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Esa Lindell returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

Rasmus Sandin is out long term and has missed the last 9 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 38% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 53:54 together.
Jack St. Ivany joined from WPG on Oct 25 and has played beside Cole Hutson.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, up from 8% last season.

story.head: The Capitals can’t afford to take penalties
paras: The Stars (8-5-1) beat Columbus 3-1 on Saturday, while the Capitals (8-5-0) lost 5-1 to Minnesota on Sunday. Going in, the Stars are fourth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Caps third in the Metropolitan (tied for 18th).

The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and play slow, tight games (lowest). They also have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st), and that could do real damage against the Capitals’ penalty kill (27th). Dallas has allowed 2.14 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Capitals get the league’s best looks (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (3rd). They also get their shots through to the net (5th), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Mikko Rantanen (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, and Jason Robertson (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind. Alex Tuch (10 G / 2 A / 12 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead. Dylan Strome (3 G / 9 A / 12 P in 13 GP) shares it.
Jake Oettinger (7-3-1 / .922 SV% in 11 GS) has been terrific for Dallas and is expected to start. Logan Thompson (5-4-0 / .898 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for Washington.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Wilson out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Johnston, Steel and Rantanen.
